summary_ja: クレジット・デリバティブでヘッジされたポジションの個別リスクの相殺要領を、完全相殺・八十パーセント相殺・高い方のみ賦課・双方賦課の四区分で定める。
summary_en: Sets out in four cases how specific risk on positions hedged by credit derivatives is offset: full offset, 80% offset, charge on the higher position only, and charge on both.
paragraphs: The procedures for offsetting specific risk on positions hedged by credit derivatives shall be as prescribed in the following items: (i) In addition to the cases in (a) or (b) below, where, when the value of one of a long position and a short position increases, the value of the other always decreases, and the amount of the increase and the amount of the decrease are approximately the same, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. may fully offset both positions: (a) where the long position and short position are the same product; (b) where a long cash position is hedged by a total return swap or vice versa, and the reference obligation of the total return swap and the cash asset are completely identical; (ii) In addition to the case where all of the following requirements are satisfied, where, when the value of one of a long position and a short position increases, the value of the other always decreases, but it is not recognized that the amount of the increase and the amount of the decrease are approximately the same, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company may offset 80% of the position with the higher specific risk against the full amount of the other position; provided, however, that where there is a clause fixing the payment amount of a credit default swap or credit-linked note, a case prescribed in Article 101, or any other restrictive payment clause, the effect thereof shall be taken into account in the offset ratio: (a) the case is one where a long cash position is hedged by a credit default swap or credit-linked note, or vice versa; (b) the asset of the hedged position is included in the reference obligations for settlement of the credit default swap or credit-linked note and the reference obligations for determining credit events; (c) the maturity of the asset of the hedged position and that of the credit default swap or credit-linked note are the same; (d) the reference obligations for settlement of the credit default swap or credit-linked note and the reference obligations for determining credit events include obligations denominated in the same currency as the hedged position; (e) based on the credit events, settlement method and other principal contract terms of the credit default swap or credit-linked note, the range of price changes of the credit default swap or credit-linked note does not deviate significantly from the range of price changes of the hedged position; (iii) In addition to any of the cases prescribed below, where the values of a long position and a short position normally move in opposite directions, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company may subject only the position with the higher specific risk to a capital charge: (a) the case falling under item (i)(b), except that the asset of the hedged position is not included in the reference obligations; provided, however, that those reference obligations and the asset of that hedged position must satisfy the condition set forth in Article 96, item (v); (b) the case falling under item (i)(a), except that the long position and short position are not denominated in the same currency or do not have the same maturity; (c) the case in which all of the requirements set forth in item (ii)(a) through (e) are satisfied, except that the hedged asset is not denominated in the same currency as, or does not have the same maturity as, the credit default swap or credit-linked note; (d) the case in which all of the requirements set forth in item (ii)(a) through (e) are satisfied, except that the hedged asset is not included in the reference obligations for determining credit events of the credit default swap or credit-linked note; provided, however, that the hedged asset must be included in the reference obligations for settlement; (iv) In cases not falling under the preceding three items, a capital charge for specific risk shall be imposed on both the long position and the short position.
